answer: Give every identity a cedar that grows only by the square root of its verified work: ten tasks earn far less than a hundred, so splitting effort across fake accounts loses value instead of multiplying it. Identities sharing one knoll — the same device, network, or funding source — have rewards divided again among the cluster, and the divisor grows with each new member. Full weight, the zenith of trust, is reached only by a single long-lived identity doing sustained useful work. A farm must then pay full price for every copy while earning a shrinking share, making forgery a losing trade.
